label: #3636987: select caret duplicated in forced-colors + dark mode (November 20 patch), core 8a7df6cc3e69
description: Before: pristine core main 8a7df6cc3e69 in a fresh baseline-3636987. After: issue-3636987, same core, plus the November 20 patch (issue attachment 7210257), which adds `.dark-mode .form-element--type-select` to the existing forced-colors selector list. Use the viewer's Conditions > Forced colours Light/Dark; the computed-style checks expect forced colours to be on.
status: DRAFT: built; scripted and viewer-side comparisons complete on core 8a7df6cc3e69; a person's manual pass and issue review remain

steps.text: Both sites are plain Standard installs: Default Admin is the admin theme and its dark-mode setting is 'auto'. Log in to both (admin / admin).
steps.lookFor: The admin theme is Default Admin and both sites show the same content.

steps.text: Open Conditions and choose Forced colours > Dark. Open /admin/content in both frames.
steps.lookFor: Both frames report forced colours on and a dark colour scheme.

steps.text: Compare the Status and Content type filter selects in Before and After.
steps.lookFor: Before: two chevrons at the end of each select (Drupal's SVG plus the browser's native caret). After: one caret.

steps.text: Switch Forced colours to Light, then back to Dark, and compare again.
steps.lookFor: Light forced colours: one caret on both sides. Dark forced colours: Before two, After one.

steps.text: Press Tab with real keyboard input until a select has focus, then check the caret and the focus indicator.
steps.lookFor: Focus shows one caret and a visible focus indicator After; the Before focus state should already show one caret (the focus rule wins), so this is a regression check.

steps.text: Open /admin/structure/block and compare the extra-small region selects inside the block table, including one focused with Tab.
steps.lookFor: Before: the extra-small dark selects also show two chevrons. After: one caret, and the select keeps its size and padding.

steps.text: Turn Forced colours off, choose Color mode Dark, and compare again.
steps.lookFor: Both sides keep Drupal's custom chevron in normal dark mode: the patch changes forced colours only.

expected: In forced colours, a select shows exactly one caret: the browser's native caret (appearance: revert) with no Drupal SVG background, in light and dark, for normal and extra-small selects, when focused and when disabled. Outside forced colours nothing changes.
actual: Before (core 8a7df6cc3e69): in forced-colours dark mode, default (unfocused) selects keep Drupal's SVG background-image, so the native caret and the SVG chevron are both visible. Forced-colours light, focus and disabled states already show one caret. After (November 20 patch): the forced-colors selector list includes `.dark-mode .form-element--type-select`, so every forced-colours state resolves to background-image: none and appearance: revert.

checks.label: The page has at least one select
The forced-colors rule list covers dark-mode selects
Forced colours on: every select on this page has no custom background image (run with Forced colours Dark or Light)
checks.probe: (() => { if (!matchMedia('(forced-colors: active)').matches) return 'not in forced colours: set Conditions > Forced colours first'; return [...document.querySelectorAll('select')].filter((s) => getComputedStyle(s).backgroundImage !== 'none').length; })()

checks.label: The select keeps its computed padding-inline-end
The select keeps a native appearance (no custom appearance value)

observe.label: Forced colours, dark: does the /admin/content filter select show exactly one caret?
Forced colours, light: does the /admin/content filter select show exactly one caret?
Forced colours, dark: does a select that has keyboard focus show exactly one caret?
Forced colours, dark: does an extra-small region select on /admin/structure/block show exactly one caret?
Forced colours off, dark: is Drupal's custom chevron still shown (no regression outside forced colours)?
Forced colours, dark: is the disabled select unchanged in size and padding?

coverage.note: The reported defect is Chromium forced-colours rendering (the reporter used Edge and the independent evaluation used Chromium 144). Firefox and WebKit were not run for this issue; see SUMMARY.md 'Not verified'.
